judged_text: The duplicate filter compares guest input to stored attendee emails with case-sensitive === even though email identity is case-insensitive, so a case-variant of an existing attendee passes as unique. Submitting 'John@Corp.com' when 'john@corp.com' is already an attendee reaches createMany and breaks the booking's attendee-email identity — an unhandled Prisma P2002 surfaces as a raw 500 toast where the (bookingId,email) unique constraint exists, and duplicate attendee rows that receive every subsequent booking email twice where it does not.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe check uses a case-sensitive comparison: `guest === attendee.email` inside `uniqueGuests` filtering. Because emails are generally treated as case-insensitive identifiers, a case-variant like `John@Corp.com` will not be filtered out when `john@corp.com` already exists, allowing a logical duplicate to proceed into `attendees.createMany`. The code also lowercases the blacklist entries but compares them to `guest` without lowercasing, so case-variants can bypass the blacklist as well. The later behavior about Prisma `P2002`/DB uniqueness is not shown in the diff, but the case-sensitive dedupe itself is a concrete correctness issue introduced here.
